summary: Single-binary command-line tool that lets AI agents create, read and edit Word, Excel and PowerPoint files without Office.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OfficeCLI is an Office suite built for AI agents. It's a single binary with no Office installation or dependencies that can create, read and edit .docx, .xlsx and .pptx files, and render them to HTML or PNG so agents can see the result.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents struggle to produce well-formatted Office documents. OfficeCLI gives them precise commands and a renderer to check their work.
whoFor: Teams generating Office files in pipelines
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a dependency-free binary with a skill file agents can install themselves, structured JSON output and high-fidelity rendering.

overview: For agents, paste curl -fsSL https://officecli.ai/SKILL.md into your agent's chat; the skill file teaches it to install and use OfficeCLI.
For people, install with the script, Homebrew (brew install officecli), npm (npm install -g @officecli/officecli) or a binary from GitHub Releases. Windows uses a PowerShell script.
Commands include create, add (slides, shapes with properties), view as outline or HTML, and get elements as JSON. OfficeCLI is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Complex layouts may need several commands

install.verificationNote: Commands come from OfficeCLI's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

firstRun.title: Create a slide deck
firstRun.code:
officecli create deck.pptx
officecli add deck.pptx / --type slide --prop title="Q4 Report" --prop background=1A1A2E

tutorial.title: Build and preview a slide
tutorial.useCase: Create a deck, add text and view it.

steps.title: Create and add a slide
steps.code:
officecli create deck.pptx
officecli add deck.pptx / --type slide --prop title="Q4 Report" --prop background=1A1A2E

steps.title: Add a text box
steps.code:
officecli add deck.pptx '/slide[1]' --type shape \
  --prop text="Revenue grew 25%" --prop x=2cm --prop y=5cm \
  --prop font=Arial --prop size=24 --prop color=FFFFFF

tutorial.expected: A rendered preview of your slide opens in the browser.
nextSteps: Let your agent install the skill
